question: Should socket.drain preserve existing slow-subscriber drop behavior by default, or intentionally close slow Gateway clients during reset/delete/new so eviction delivery fails closed?
rationale: The mechanical type/docs fixes are clear, but the drain backpressure choice changes a public Gateway websocket compatibility and availability contract.

options.title: Preserve slow-client compatibility
options.body: Keep socket.drain targeted and documented, but pass an explicit dropIfSlow-compatible option unless a later public contract deliberately changes slow-client handling.

options.title: Approve close-on-drain
options.body: Treat eviction drains as critical control-plane frames, keep close-on-slow behavior, and document that reset/delete/new may disconnect slow subscribers.

options.title: Pause for a narrower contract
options.body: Hold this branch until the Gateway event/backpressure contract is split into a smaller maintainer-owned API decision.

recommendation.title: Preserve slow-client compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep socket.drain targeted and documented, but pass an explicit dropIfSlow-compatible option unless a later public contract deliberately changes slow-client handling.
